title: Microsoft Seen As 'Adults In Charge' Of AI. Stock Upgraded To Buy.
source_used: Investor's Business Daily (first paragraph only, the rest is behind its subscription wall); Stocktwits (citing TheFly) on TradingView for the analyst's reasoning. Benzinga blocked (Cloudflare 403).
key_facts: Melius Research analyst Ben Reitzes upgraded Microsoft stock to buy from hold on Monday 5 Oct 2026 and raised his price target to $665 from $465 (IBD).
IBD: the upgrade came as the software giant is seen as a leader in trustworthiness when it comes to AI; Microsoft rose 1.5% to close at $525.18.
Stocktwits, citing TheFly: Melius said Microsoft and cybersecurity companies could become increasingly important as AI leaders discuss the risks of the technology.
Melius also said enterprises are spending on a secure wrapper that can route models to the right task and secure AI agents.
Separately, Scotiabank raised its Microsoft target to $615 from $510 with an 'Outperform' rating; Wells Fargo recently raised its target to $725 from $700.
Microsoft said Azure and other cloud services revenue grew 43% year on year in its fiscal fourth quarter and Microsoft 365 Copilot passed 30 million paid seats.
quote_evidence: Microsoft (MSFT) stock scored an upgrade on Monday as the software giant is seen as a leader in trustworthiness when it comes to artificial intelligence.
Melius Research analyst Ben Reitzes upgraded Microsoft stock to buy from hold.
He raised his price target to 665 from 465.
why_it_matters_hint: One research firm's rating change gave Microsoft shares a lift; it is an opinion, not new company results.
notes: IBD page returns only its first paragraph (paywall). Further detail from Stocktwits on TradingView, which cites the news service TheFly. The 'from 465' prior target appears only in IBD's text. Analyst opinion, not a company announcement.
